findings.title: From an unsettled interval to dense confinement
findings.claim: The temporal movement can also be pictured spatially: a briefly held, unsettled interval gives way to forced movement and a dense, resistant destination.
findings.mechanism: 31:10 pairs rooted mountains with earth that may sway. That distinct stability-versus-motion image returns through the focus's little interval, compelled movement, directional endpoint, and physical-thickness branch, allowing the sequence to be visualized as a shift from unsettled ground into dense confinement.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive a spatial transition alongside the literal movement from enjoyment to punishment.
findings.containment: This remains an exploratory analogy, not a lexical claim that qalilan means motion or that punishment is physically dense. The 31:10 roles and roots are legacy-attributed, and the packet does not establish an intentional echo.

findings.title: An enforced cutoff from granted benefit
findings.claim: The focus's brief grant followed by compelled punishment can be pictured as an enforced weaning: access to the prior benefit ends, and that deprivation becomes one strand of the pain.
findings.mechanism: 31:14 explicitly mentions a child's weaning and separation after nurture. The focus places granted enjoyment before thumma, compulsion, and punishment. Contact between that distinct cutoff image and the focus's forced transition activates withholding as an analogy while preserving punishment as the direct destination.
findings.reader_payoff: The ending of the granted benefit becomes part of the transition, not merely a separate event added afterward.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory image, not a lexical definition of punishment and not a claim that 31:14 intentionally foreshadows 31:24. The context root and role are attributed and remain without a registered branch gloss.

friction_notes: Focus word alignment resolves all seven analysis words to QAC; no focus carrier is dropped for a missing analysis join.
The 2:126 connection supplies exact Arabic but no target morphology or target-side lexicon record; the cross-surah echo is assessed at surface level only.
The wider HFT coordinates and roles for 31:6, 31:8–10, 31:14–15, 31:20–23, and 31:26–27 remain legacy-attributed even where exact Arabic is supplied.
Whether qalilan primarily limits quantity, duration, or both remains open; neither the repeated sequence nor the abundance contrast resolves it.
The spatial and forced-weaning readings remain exploratory analogies and do not establish intentional local echoes.
The support that invokes 31:29, 31:33, and post-rescue denial names those contexts without exact anchored surfaces or word traces, so those mechanisms are excluded from the global findings.
